contract: docs/ARCHITECTURE_CONTRACT.md sections A.42 (RC-58), A.43 (RC-59), A.45 (RC-61) and A.46 (RC-62)
notes: Each case is one Evidence-ready Candidate forming one EventGroup. report_period decides, through the production cadence owner, whether the run carries the monthly monitored-standards check.
category_id is the Classifier outcome under section L, which RC-58 and RC-59 do not change. source_date is the document's own date for TemporalRule.
expected is the domain outcome of the case's own Evidence: the Scope state and basis, date validity, the monitored standard, the Reportability state and reason, and the report section.

helper_answers are the semantically correct helper answers for that Evidence, so the production owners can be executed. ordinary_scope is the existing urban-rail Scope answer. NOT_CALLED means Python must decide without that question.
The region rule (RC-28) and Delivery are executed on the existing region fixtures and report fakes in tests/test_monitored_standards.py.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a monitored standard publishes a new edition
cases.source_content: The IEC published the third edition of IEC 61373 for shock and vibration tests of rolling stock equipment used on metro and railway vehicles. The new edition replaces the 2010 edition and revises the test levels for bogie-mounted equipment.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a monitored standard opens a formal draft for public comment
cases.source_content: NFPA opened the public comment period on the first draft of the next edition of NFPA 130, Standard for Fixed Guideway Transit and Passenger Rail Systems. Comments on the draft revisions to tunnel ventilation and emergency egress requirements are accepted until the stated closing date.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a monitored standard is only required by a metro procurement
cases.source_content: The metro operator awarded the signalling replacement contract for Line 2 to a named supplier. The contract requires the supplier to demonstrate compliance with EN 50126 and EN 50129 before commissioning.

cases.scenario: monthly check: formal metro guidance only mentions a monitored standard
cases.source_content: The transport ministry issued formal fire-safety guidance to all metro operators with an implementation date next year. The guidance notes that NFPA 130 remains the reference for station egress design.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a regulation makes compliance with a monitored standard mandatory; the standard itself is unchanged
cases.source_content: The rail regulator adopted a binding rule that makes compliance with EN 50128 mandatory for new metro signalling software from next year. EN 50128 itself is not revised by the rule.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a standard outside the monitored list is revised
cases.source_content: The IEC published a revised edition of IEC 62290-1 on management and command/control systems for urban guided transport. The revision updates the grades of automation used by metro operators.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a city ordinance on subway safety is amended
cases.source_content: The city council amended the ordinance on subway platform safety to require gap-warning devices at curved platforms. The amended ordinance takes effect in March.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a metro deployment is tested to a monitored standard
cases.source_content: The metro completed trial running of its new onboard condition-monitoring units on Line 5. The units were tested to IEC 61373 before installation.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a national body publishes its adoption of an amendment to a monitored part (RC-61: not a change of the standard)
cases.source_content: BSI published amendment A1 to BS EN 50122-2:2010, which revises the stray-current limits for DC traction systems.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a monitored standard's interim amendment never mentions urban rail
cases.source_content: The NFPA Standards Council issued a tentative interim amendment to NFPA 70 that revises the ground-fault protection requirements of Section 210.8. The amendment applies to the current edition of the code.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a regional body outside the designated regions makes a monitored IEC edition available (RC-61: not IEC's own change)
cases.source_content: CENELEC in Brussels made available a new edition of IEC 60076-11 for dry-type power transformers. The new edition supersedes the 2018 edition.

cases.scenario: an ordinary week: the same interim amendment is not checked, and general Scope still applies
cases.source_content: The NFPA Standards Council issued a tentative interim amendment to NFPA 70 that revises the ground-fault protection requirements of Section 210.8. The amendment applies to the current edition of the code.

cases.scenario: monthly check for November: a monitored change dated in December belongs to the December check
cases.source_content: The IEC published amendment 1 to IEC 62271-100 for high-voltage alternating-current circuit-breakers.

cases.scenario: monthly check: an article merely mentions a monitored standard and no urban rail
cases.source_content: An electrical-trade article explains how NFPA 70 applies to fire safety in data centers. It describes the requirements of the current edition.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a city ordinance that names no urban rail cannot use the monitored basis
cases.source_content: The city council amended its building ordinance to require sprinklers in new parking garages. The amendment takes effect next year.

cases.scenario: monthly check: the issuing body outside the designated regions amends a monitored EN part (RC-61)
cases.source_content: CENELEC in Brussels published amendment A1 to EN 50122-2, which revises the stray-current limits for DC traction systems.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a national body publishes its adoption of a monitored IEC edition (RC-61: not a second update)
cases.source_content: BSI published BS EN IEC 61373:2026, the UK adoption of IEC 61373:2026 on shock and vibration tests for railway rolling stock equipment.

cases.scenario: monthly check: a regional body publishes its adoption of a monitored IEC edition (RC-61: not a second update)
cases.source_content: CENELEC published EN IEC 61373:2026, the European adoption of IEC 61373:2026 on shock and vibration tests for railway rolling stock equipment.

cases.scenario: monthly check: IEC changes a numbered part of a monitored series that no family coverage lists (RC-62: numbering alone is not monitoring)
cases.source_content: The IEC published the fourth edition of IEC 60076-5, which specifies the ability of power transformers to withstand short circuit.

cases.scenario: monthly check: IEC changes a numbered part of a withdrawn monitored identifier that no family coverage lists (RC-62)
cases.source_content: The IEC published an amendment to IEC 60332-1-2, the test procedure for vertical flame propagation of a single insulated cable.

cases.scenario: monthly check: CENELEC revises a part that succeeded a withdrawn monitored identifier; no family coverage lists it (RC-62: a split is not coverage)
cases.source_content: CENELEC published a new edition of EN 50126-1, the generic RAMS process for railway applications.

cases.scenario: monthly check: CENELEC amends a sibling part of an explicitly listed child; no family coverage lists it (RC-62)
cases.source_content: CENELEC published amendment A1 to EN 50122-1, which revises the protective provisions against electric shock for fixed traction installations.
